key_insight: Pretrained vehicle-aerodynamics surrogates transfer unreliably, while GeoReplay preserves source-domain accuracy without sacrificing fine-tuning’s target accuracy.
engineering_relevance: GeoReplay could make surrogate adaptation to new vehicle classes more reusable while limiting loss of accuracy on previously modeled vehicles.
method: Benchmark five DrivAerML-pretrained surrogates on four independent target datasets.
Replay source simulations with geometries resembling the target, applying their updates only when aligned with the target gradient.
Separate geometric coverage from simulated-physics differences in a risk bound and prove target-training descent for sufficiently small GeoReplay steps.
evidence_signal: Across datasets differing in geometry, CFD solver, turbulence model, and flow conditions, fine-tuning beat training from scratch in fewer than half of comparisons; GeoReplay reduced fine-tuning’s source error in 77 of 80 settings while matching target accuracy.
watch_item: GeoReplay requires retained source simulations and gradient-alignment checks; its target-training descent guarantee does not establish generalization to unseen vehicles.
paper_title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics
